Status.note: Evergy announced on May 12, 2026 that it began construction of the plant in northwest Sumner County and held a groundbreaking. KWCH television reported the groundbreaking the next day. Evergy's own second quarter 2026 filing to the Missouri Public Service Commission also describes construction work on site. GEM shows pre-construction.

Capacity (MW).note: Evergy's release, its Missouri filing and its Kansas rate petition all call this a 710 MW combined cycle plant. The air permit application says about 720 MW gross and 705 MW net. GEM shows 765 MW, which is the nameplate in the EIA-860M table. Evergy's 710 MW is the figure to use.

Other Name(s).note: Evergy unveiled the official name Chisholm Trail Energy Center at the May 12, 2026 groundbreaking. It replaces the project name Viola.

Start year.note: Evergy says the plant will be operating in 2029. GEM already has 2029, so this is unchanged.

Status Detail.value: In May 2026, Evergy began construction and held a groundbreaking for the plant, now named Chisholm Trail Energy Center. Evergy expects it to operate in 2029. Kiewit Power Constructors is the builder and the turbine is a Mitsubishi M501JAC. Evergy Missouri West and Evergy Kansas Central each own half.
Status Detail.note: New text for the top of the box. The existing text, which says construction is expected to begin in late 2026 or early 2027, stays below it.

units.notes: The status change is supported by Evergy's release and local television news from the next day. Evergy's Missouri filing for the second quarter of 2026 gives the steam turbine drain pit and tower crane foundations as examples of work done.

City.note: KWCH describes the plant as near Conway Springs. The state air permit notice puts the site about five miles southwest of Conway Springs. The mail town is Conway Springs, zip 67031.

Location accuracy.note: The coordinates in GEM fall in an open farm field in the satellite picture I took, with no plant on it. The picture is older than the May 2026 groundbreaking. Three documents place the site within about 400 meters of each other: GEM's point, the Evergy rate petition and the air permit application. None is a parcel map, so I cannot call the point exact. I did not move the point.

qa.recommendation: I could not pin the exact month of the pre-construction step. The Missouri Public Service Commission order granting the certificate is dated July 31, 2025, and the Kansas Corporation Commission approved the cost principles in July 2025. The Kansas air permit notice ran until November 24, 2025. Please use July 2025 as the earliest firm date.
qa.note: Answer to the validation report question about step dates.

qa.recommendation: Evergy's May 2025 plan update has five placeholder plants named Evergy Kansas Central 2025 IRP power station 1 to 5. The 355 MW Kansas Central share of this plant appears in the 2029 column of that plan, so one placeholder may duplicate this plant. Please check and remove the placeholder if so. Crooked Creek in Wilson County is a different plant.
qa.note: Plan decks show only chart totals, so I could not match a placeholder to this plant for sure.

qa.recommendation: GEM shows 765 MW from the EIA-860M table. Evergy, its filings and its permit documents give 710 MW. Please confirm the change to 710 MW in the web form.
qa.note: Also covered by the proposed capacity edit.
